text: 「从若此后百年千年，来人漫步于繁星身侧，人们便要赞颂她的名。」
星象学家们穷极一生为星座与天体赋予象征意义，萨满和德鲁伊们试图解释每一道流星留下的痕迹。
触不可及。正因为触不可及，天空才是湎于幻想之人的归宿。对于这片大地，抬头仰望毫无意义。
「遥不可及的东西时而会成为你的道标。」
「如果你想做正确的事，首先你要知道什么是正确的。其次，你要知道，并不是做正确的事情就不需要付出代价。」
「再坚固的‘基石’，也只能铸就其他人前行的路。」
「只是荒唐的事情发生得太有条理，以至于看起来像是我们真的在变好似的。」
理想，偏执，好奇，进取。科学家们总与这些品质联系在一起。
哥伦比亚荒野的雨后，植物总是会疯长。我不喜欢人们以居高临下的态度判断，哪些植物有用，哪些植物该被贬为杂草。
「从来没有人质疑日升月落，也没有人质疑万物生长。」
「雅拉主任，这世上从来没有装在玻璃罩里的‘纯粹的科学’。科学在我们的手掌中，在人的手掌中。」
那些人永远声称自己是在前进，可他们只是胡乱把脚伸向自己想践踏的地方而已。
但你没办法让他们停下的。你自己也是研究者，你知道什么最无法阻挡——是渴求。
这片大地上，从古至今，在克丽斯腾之前，你说的那些贪婪的、狂妄的、冒进的、顽固的人们，他们又何曾停下过？
雅拉主任，我觉得——科学的燃料不该是欲望与理想，也不该是计算与取舍。科学是真切地看向每一个人。
但也必须有人站出来，确保科学——依然在人的手中。
我把最后的血给了她，供养一颗新的心脏，也许好过守着一盏将熄的灯。这只是婴儿好奇的一瞥——却要跨越什么样的阻碍？
可是，现在，每个人都在抬头仰望，抬头仰望那道连接天与地的光束。仰望着从来便触不可及的天空。
「但科学绝不是神，科学是供人通行的道路罢了。它需时时被审视，时时被修缮，时时被规范。」
「我们都被她所吸引……从一开始，我们就是一起上的路。如果我承认我的羸弱和犹疑，那么，跟随那个真正强大的灵魂，也是一种选择，对吧？」
「即使简陋如玩具，次生文明第一次突破天空的长矛也足以让这个幼小的世界瞠目结舌。」
人们还远远没有意识到团结的重要性，也无法从根本上抛弃差异与旧日的仇恨去谈论和平与未来。
团结是一个永恒的难题。时至今日还有人叫嚣着历史中的战争，而从不肯正视那些苦难和那些枉死的人。他们甚至看不见这句话。
「假设确实有一个更高意志存在，是它划定了边界，决定了人类的未来和去路——那在决定成为仆从还是举起反旗之前，我们不都该尝试着直视它的眼睛吗？」
科学家不相信梦是假的。因为他们会向全人类证明，所有的梦都可能成真。
「我多希望……多希望我们始终都坐在一起，就在那片星光熠熠的黑夜里。但我没有办法同时拉住你们两个。三个人的舞……终究还是太难跳了。」
对他们来说，每一次星星的运行轨迹发生改变，就是一次新的启示、一个有意义的预兆。
相信群星不过是某个不可知存在手中的棋子，它的运转以及它轨迹的改变都是有其意义的，显然要让人安心得多。
数颗星星互相碰撞，虽然没有碎裂，但是碰撞产生的响声一瞬间破坏了室内的静谧。「伪造的。」
「如果群星移动的轨迹真的无迹可寻，那么在过去漫长的时光中，我们又是如何避免与其他星星碰撞的呢？我们特殊至此吗？我们究竟生活在怎样的一片土地上？我们将前往何处？」
整条银河正朝着塞雷娅倾泻而下。星星与大地相撞。满地洁白的碎屑中，一个人抬起头来。
我敬佩他们的意志和决心。可我从来都无法赞同理所当然的牺牲。他们很多人都以为我过于保守。他们认为我拘泥于规则，始终都在阻挠你们前进。
「因为人类对前进的渴望本就不可战胜。这是一种欲望，一种‘疯狂’，可也是生命的本能，是我们从一无所有的荒野里走到此时此地的燃料。」
沉重的星星们如落石般砸向她，引力操控着气流在她周身呼啸。钙质结晶从头到脚一点点碎裂，但登山者决心以血肉之躯迎接风暴。
于是在来这里的路上，我回顾了……我们所有人的起点。是的，我畏惧失控，其实并非是畏惧混乱，而是畏惧混乱导致的倒退。
「……是啊，时至今日，人们依然生活在黑夜里。毕竟……我们就连头顶的天幕都看不穿。」
「真正的先驱者，应该为全人类开道，而不是率先跳进深渊，有去无回。这就是我的源头，我要确保的东西。」
「到圣山去。我们从出生开始，就只有这一个目的。我们童年时在留有青苔的平原上与树木嬉戏，向岩石学习，步入青壮之后，便要开始着手攀登高山。」
「道阻且长，我们只能取材自山谷之间，所幸圣山仁慈，它用死亡喂养我们，而我们将漫长的一生贡献给这条山路，以作回报。」
「……这座山名唤‘时间’，而我们？我们只是渺小的生命。时间总是伟大的，不是吗？你应该最清楚不过。」
「我不知道。我不知道的意思就是——也许会。试着对时间的空谷呼喊吧。你得到的回应就是圣山的恩赐。」
「我见过数千年的战争，国家兴起，诸国并立，人们在隔阂与冲突中变化。但最终，他们皆如萨尔贡的黄沙般随风逝去。」
「永远不会有足够‘充分’的准备。假如灾难确实悬于头顶，那所有的人类都活在倒计时里。」
亘古的双月露出真容。今夜，真实终于被人类首次窥见。这一夜，无数艺术家彻夜未眠。这一夜，阴谋在小巷中诞生，无数政治家辗转反侧。
「我的父母始终坚定地向自己的目标迈进，他们最终只是输给了自己。如果旅程注定无法到达终点，那么我同样愿意死在途中。」
「那会是一片索拉里斯之海。一切都会在无序中存续。」
「寻找的过程是无价的，而找到答案以后，人们便只会歌颂答案。」
「我们无法理解，我们无法交流，我们是两道波频完全相异的电波。」
「没有什么现实是无法改变的，没有什么牺牲是理所当然的。如果大部分人只能被迫在梦想与现实间做个选择，那么，我必须成为梦想与现实之间的桥梁。」
「苦难、战争、天灾与摧毁一切的傲慢，思潮与理想，被赋予的伟大和生来的平等，这片渺小旷野上诞生的文明与我们曾经无比热爱的一切……它们唯一注定的意义和生命最终的求索，是什么？」「未来。」
These stars have shone at the zenith of Terra since ancient times. How much romantic myth they carry, and how many searching eyes.
The distant tower held clouds in its vast glass facade, strangely clear, like a leaf brimming with dew. It was, in fact, only a leaf.
Look up and the sky is so vast that the whole of Trimont is no more than a single thin leaf.
Trimont was planned with great care; though the towers stand crowded, they are staggered to avoid shadowing one another, and the early winter sun still falls evenly on every street.
You look up: a dark cloud drifts slowly far away, the wind blows toward it, and it seems to move farther from the city with every moment.
She is Liberi, she is Fedia. The night wind is her carriage, the stars her partners in the dance. She is the last of the god-kin on this land who has not lost the power of the sky.
A scientist needs to consider only one thing: how to achieve it. A scientist need only push science forward, and that one thing alone is enough to exhaust us completely.
You must know its temperature, its weight, whether it burns, and what pain or solace it will bring.
But, Hemo, this is progress. No one knows where the road is, so they simply walk. The lucky find the right place and step into the light; the unlucky wander in circles down dead ends.
Matter cannot bind it, morality cannot bind it, and rules cannot bind it either.
Then from now on they must stop. At least until they truly bend down and see what lies beneath their feet, they must stop.
Science must advance, and it will advance. Perhaps some, the Chief among them, are better at the advancing part.
Help a small animal with its mad plan? Or witness a young civilization take its first step out of the cradle?
Once, for this land, looking up meant nothing. That place was not worth observing and not worth exploring; it was the refuge of those lost in fantasy.
Among the stars, that tiny man-made thing, so small in the flow of light, is brewing the ambition of humanity in this age.
What it should bring us is not the magnificent future of a madman's fantasy, but the ordinary expectations of ordinary people.
I can still catch up to her, and she must shine. The one who transcends has set out on her journey; I think she does not mind a timid hitchhiker following along her long road.
The threat of the ocean grows by the day, yet the mighty Aegir civilization clings to its arrogance. They still have strength to spare, and still they underestimate the sea.
But these are only lands beyond the soil of civilization; they were never the direct cause that strangles the future. Division and prejudice, war and strife.
Even as the cataclysm descended, the arsenals of Ursus never stopped for a moment, and the farmers of Kazimierz still bore their crushing levies.
If you want to reach a certain future, you must first open a dialogue with the end, rather than force a route upon it.
I do not believe in every law I have been told. I do not believe humanity can never pierce the Starpod, still less that the stars are as small as they appear.
She tried to find Muelsyse, but deep in every surging current there seemed to hide an elf's eyes, calm and sorrowful eyes. The water roared, and the elf wept.
Compared with the other side, crowded with instruments, this place was more like a temple of stars. The metal of the spheres was flawless and revealed a startling beauty under the soft light.
One by one, spheres of every size moved slowly along their appointed orbits, and every so often those orbits would change.

These irregularities crossed one another and formed an indescribable harmony. In the placing of the stars and the precision of their shifting orbits, this orrery surpassed anything an astrologer could imagine.
So-called astrologers are little different from blind fools. For thousands of years they have devoted themselves to tracing the movements of the stars.
Their behavior is not incomprehensible. The fact that the stars move without any trace is enough to unsettle most people.
Kristen reached toward the orrery. The dome over the Garden of Stars opened suddenly, and false starlight poured unchecked into the laboratory.
Fake. The trajectories of the stars began to fall into chaos. Wrong.
Yet Kristen's eyes did not change in the least, as though everything were exactly as it should be.
These questions... I have repeated them in your ear far too many times.

But science should be rational. Had they not died in that accident, had they turned back before striking the barrier, they would have brought people priceless data and the possibility of another attempt.
Truth arises from the inertia of pursuing order. I believe science brings truth, and truth restrains madness and brings a better order to humanity.
So I did not come here to oppose you.
Kristen, on my way to find you I nearly admitted defeat. Then someone told me I needed to find my way back to the source.
I must go forward; humanity must go forward. For us, the long march is far from over.
Those of us who know more must carry more responsibility. We should walk ahead of others, clear the dangers from their path, and lead them forward carefully.
She crossed the galaxy and passed through the storm.
We need many preparations at the foot of the mountain: twisting the dawn light strand by strand into rope, or a pair of shoes the night cannot stain. Then we begin to climb.
Hardship? No, no, no. Snow does not grieve at melting. All of that is other people's sentimentality; we simply climb.
Will the mountain change? Has anyone ever reached the summit?
This is no meaningless act. Time will not answer of its own accord, but time does respond. Those before us called that response fate; fate is the echo of life crying out to time.

When I first learned of the universe from Friston, I could not imagine it held a sight so vast, majestic, beautiful and moving. It surpasses our vision and the poor imagination we built on the known; no language describes it exactly.

In a world still coming apart, where the divides of ideology and race push civilization toward self-destruction, where peace and unity are illusions beyond reach, the most direct path is to use those powers to reshape the will of every living thing and make them one.
She believed that one day this land would need people able to stand together beyond politics and race. These far-sighted ones would have to use everything at hand to build an ark.
The only ones who can ever save the people of Terra are the people themselves. That need to awaken is eternal, simply because all of them are human.
The sky was torn open at one corner and the truth was laid before everyone; we have no reason to ignore it. But even if every head is raised, the problems underfoot do not simply vanish.
The clouds moved fast, and one star appeared faintly in the dusk. The sky was as high and distant as ever. ...Safe travels.
Good night, then, to all of you on Terra. Good night, universe.
